text:
alex: heads-up — seeing a write latency spike on a subset of local NVMe hosts in us-west-2, lots of kernel writeback stalls and `blk_update_request: I/O error` noise in dmesg.
maria: Oof. Any particular instance group or fleet tag? :grimacing:
alex: nvme-local-pool-2 (gp3-backed hosts) — ~40% of nodes showing avgqu-sz > 20 and %util approaching 100% for nvme0n1.
kevin: Can you paste `iostat` / `nvme` output? Might be a sudden write amplification from older batches.
alex: sure, quick capture:

```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device:         rrqm/s wrqm/s   r/s   w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1           0.00  60.00  12.0 1200.0  512.0 61440.0   100.0   32.5  25.0   0.5  25.0  0.8  96.0
```
alex: and kernel log excerpt:

```
[ 1234.567890] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 12345678
[ 1234.567892] Buffer I/O error on dev nvme0n1, logical block 1543209
```
jamie: Looks more like saturation than flash failure so far (errors could be timeouts from queueing). Any big evict/cleaner jobs running? those scrub/cleanup tasks are noisy right now.
maria: yep, ephemeral-cleaner cron kicked off across the pool at 02:12 UTC — it's aggressively rewriting objects to reclaim space. That matches the timeline.
kevin: If the cleaner is doing small random writes it will destroy throughput on older NVMe — we should throttle it. Can we pause it for affected nodes and instruct it to do longer sleep between batches?
alex: proposing immediate mitigation: 1) stop ephemeral-cleaner on impacted hosts, 2) temporarily route heavy write jobs to dedicated write-pool, 3) bump queue_depth and reduce iosched writeback window. Thoughts?
infra-oncall: I can stop the cleaner now on nodes tagged `ephemeral-hot-2`. Running `systemctl stop ephemeral-cleaner.service` and setting `ENV_EPHEMERAL_CLEANER_RATE=50` for rate limiting.
jamie: +1 to stop and rate-limit. Also try `echo 64 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/nr_requests` on a single host as test, and monitor tail latency.
kevin: We should also avoid a mass restart — do it in waves 5 nodes at a time so we don't cause eviction storms. I'll open a quick playbook.
maria: I'll update the routing policy so new batch jobs avoid `nvme-local-pool-2` until we confirm stable. That'll cut write pressure by ~30% per historic traffic patterns.
alex: after stopping cleaner on 5 hosts, avgqu-sz dropped to ~6 and %util to ~55 within 90s. Pulling metrics to dashboards now.
sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-3524 — "nvme local write saturation us-west-2". Pager duty notified to infra-oncall.
infra-oncall: rolling mitigation done for first wave (5/20 hosts). Will monitor for 10min then proceed.
jamie: we should add an on-host rate limiter for future (cgroup blkio throttle or `ionice -c2 -n7`) so background reclaim can't saturate the SSD.
kevin: long term: schedule a firmware check + replace highest SMART wear nodes. Also consider moving smaller ephemeral shards onto nvme1 namespace with less wear.
maria: note on cost/regional constraints — us-west-2 has limited spare high-iops hosts; migrating load to another region is expensive for customers pinned to data residency. We'll need a plan that doesn't rely on cross-region shift.
alex: agreed. short-term: throttle cleaner + route jobs + bump queue_depth worked. medium-term: add adaptive cleaner that monitors avgqu-sz and backs off, plus alerting on avgqu-sz > 15.
kevin: ticket for adaptive cleaner: INFRA-9135. Assigning to jamie and alex.
jamie: will prototype an adaptive backoff today.
infra-oncall: last check — write latencies back to acceptable levels. I'll keep watch for 2 hours and then reopen cleaner with rate limit of 30%.
alex: thanks all. saving logs to the incident and adding `nvme-local-pool-2` to a health-check that triggers before any cleaner run. :thumbsup:
